title: EmoGenie: Benchmarking and Evaluating Expressed and Evoked Emotion in T2I Generation with MLLMs
title_zh: EmoGenie：基于MLLMs对T2I生成中表达与激发情绪的性能基准测试与评估

paragraphs.en: EmoGenie是一个针对AI生成图像的情感基准测试，旨在评估T2I生成与MLLM理解在表达情绪和激发情绪方面的能力。 Rapid advances in artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) have significantly promoted using text-to-image (T2I) models to generate images with specific affective intentions. However, the emotional effects conveyed by generated images frequently deviate from target expectations, and it remains unclear whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can reliably interpret the emotion of AI-generated visual content. Existing affective benchmarks are predominantly built on natural images, while affective studies of generated images have largely focused on emotions expressed in portraits, lacking a unified benchmark for studying the emotions expressed and evoked by generated images. We therefore introduce EmoGenie, a benchmark of emotion for AI-generated images that evaluates capabilities in T2I generation and MLLM understanding across expressed and evoked emotions. It comprises 6,400 images generated by eight T2I models using 800 emotion-targeted prompts, annotated with question-answer (QA) pairs, termed EmoGenie-QA, and continuous human ratings, termed EmoGenie-Assess. EmoGenie-QA contains 90,000 closed-set questions in single-image and image-pair settings, as well as 1,057 open-ended questions for emotion description. EmoGenie-Assess benchmarks continuous affective and aesthetic prediction using 13,175 mean opinion scores (MOSs) aggregated from human ratings in terms of valence, arousal, dominance, and aesthetic quality. We further develop EmoProbe, which combines emotion question answering with response-aligned, dimension-specific regression heads for continuous score prediction. Experimental results show that EmoProbe achieves superior results on emotion-related QA tasks, while its affective and aesthetic predictions correlate better with human ratings, demonstrating its state-of-the-art capabilities of unified coarse-to-fine affective understanding for AI-generated images.
paragraphs.zh: EmoGenie是一个针对AI生成图像的情感基准测试，旨在评估T2I生成与MLLM理解在表达情绪和激发情绪方面的能力。人工智能生成内容（AIGC）的快速发展极大地推动了文本到图像（T2I）模型在具有特定情感意图的情况下生成图像的应用。 然而，生成图像所传达的情感效果经常偏离预期目标，目前尚不清楚多模态大型语言模型（MLLMs）是否能够可靠地解读AI生成的视觉内容中的情感。 现有的情感基准测试主要基于自然图像构建，而针对生成图像的情感研究大多集中在肖像中表达的情感上，缺乏一个统一的标准来研究生成图像所表达和激发的情感。 因此，我们提出了EmoGenie——一个用于AI生成图像的情感基准测试，它评估了T2I生成与MLLM理解在情感表达与激发方面的能力。 该基准测试包含由八种T2I模型使用800个情感目标提示生成的6,400张图像，并标注了问答（QA）对（称为EmoGenie-QA）以及连续的人类评分（称为EmoGenie-Assess）。 EmoGenie-QA包含90,000个单图或图像对比场景下的封闭集问题，以及1,057个用于情感描述的开放性问题。 EmoGenie-Assess通过13,175个来自人类评分的平均意见得分（MOSs）来评估连续的情感与美学预测，这些得分涵盖了情感倾向、唤醒度、主导性和美学质量等方面。 我们进一步开发了EmoProbe，它将情感问答与响应对齐的、针对特定维度的回归头相结合，以实现连续分数的预测。 实验结果表明，EmoProbe在情感相关的问答任务中取得了更优的结果，其情感与美学预测也与人类评分的相关性更高，证明了其在AI生成图像的统一粗到细情感理解方面的领先水平。
